description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms

About this team and role:

Mozilla Communications, Marketing and Policy (CMP) Team is looking for an operator to make sure the entire team runs smoothly. That covers budget, people, process, offsites, templates, tools and the systems underneath all of them. The team has grown quickly across brand, product marketing, media, creative, communications and policy, and its operations have not kept pace with the work.

This is a hands-on, technically fluent operations role. The largest part of the job is the tools and automations the team uses to run itself, so that budget tracking, onboarding, planning, partner management and everyday workflows take less manual effort and hold up as the team changes. You will choose and set up those tools, build the automations, and get the team using them. The wider marketing technology and data stack stays with our MarTech team, and you will work closely with them.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the tools the team uses to run itself (project and workflow management, budget and spend tracking, partner and contract records, shared knowledge, AI assistants), and decide what gets added or retired.
  • Keep the team's operational data and shared sources of truth (budget, headcount, partners, projects, the contract library, planning and process folders) accurate, current, and in one place, so no one is reconciling spreadsheets by hand.
  • Lead the team's automation program: design and build AI agents and automated workflows that take manual effort out of how the team operates, and set the guardrails, ownership, and maintenance for the automations staff build themselves.
  • Run the marketing budget cycle in partnership with our Finance lead: set up annual envelopes by function, keep spend tracking current, support monthly reconciliation and forecasting, and run the spend approval process so every dollar has an owner and a line.
  • Own people operations for the team with our People partners: new hire onboarding, the org chart, headcount and open roles, and the basics every new team member needs on day one.
  • Own the marketing operations process, playbooks and templates, keep them current, and train the team on them.
  • Run the partner contract process for marketing: draft SOWs and change orders with the team that owns each agency, technology or creator partner, move them through review to signature, track renewals, and run partner onboarding and regular reviews against scope and cost.
  • Run the team's learning program with function leads, who keep ownership of craft: bring in new ideas, tools and ways of working through training, outside speakers and shared examples, so the team keeps building its skills.
  • Plan and run team offsites and working sessions, and support all hands meetings and other core team communication moments, from budget and logistics through the materials behind them.
  • Make sure the CMO is reporting on the team's key metrics properly: set the standard view, collect each function's numbers on time, and have it ready for monthly, QBR and board reporting. The analysis behind the numbers stays with the functions and data science.
  • Own and drive CMP’s business rhythms including annual planning, QBRs, board presentations, and monthly ET business reviews.
  • Run the mechanics of annual and quarterly planning: the calendar, the templates and the inputs each function owes, in partnership with the marketing leaders who set the plan itself.
  • Bring the team's tool and automation needs to the MarTech and web teams, who own the wider marketing technology and data stack.
  • Lead and develop a small operations team – the CMO Office.
  • Report directly to the Chief Marketing Officer.

What you’ll bring: 

  • 10+ years in marketing operations or business operations, including at least 3 years leading operations for a marketing organization of 50 or more people
  • A track record of building team systems with AI and automation tools, with examples of what you built and what it replaced. Expect to show how you use these tools during the interview process
  • Hands-on with automation platforms, AI assistants and agents, and the everyday tools a marketing team runs on, and comfortable connecting them without waiting on engineering
  • Care with data privacy and security when setting up tools and automations
  • Experience running marketing budget processes in partnership with Finance: planning, tracking, reconciliation and approvals
  • Experience managing the contract process for agency, media and technology partners, including SOWs, change orders and renewals
  • Experience with people operations for a team: onboarding, headcount tracking and working alongside HR partners
  • Strong program management across many workstreams at once, including offsites and team events
  • A record of building process that stayed in use after launch, and of training a team on a new way of working
  • The standing to hold a standard with senior leaders, and the judgment to know when a decision belongs with someone else
  • Experience working across US and European markets, time zones and cultures, previous remote work experience a must to drive program and processes
  • Clear, plain written communication
  • Commitment to our values:
    • Welcoming differences
    • Being relationship-minded
    • Practicing responsible participation
    • Having grit

What you’ll get:

  • Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team
  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)
  • Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together
  • Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday
  • One-time home office stipend
  • Annual professional development budget
  • Quarterly well-being stipend
  • Considerable paid parental leave
  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

About Mozilla 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission.  We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws.  Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose.
